Title: Saturday

My Review: A very descriptive day in the life of a neurosurgeon. I could not relate to the family because they felt implausible, but the emotions are conveyed quite well. Also, why is he hornier than a teenager?

Title: The Road
Author: Cormac McCarthy
My Review: Nerve-racking and atmospheric. The story feels dreadful to the point that death seems like a viable alternative.

Title: Fooled by Randomness: The Hidden Role of Chance in Life and in the Markets (Incerto)
Author: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
My Review: A very chewable and fun introduction to uncertainty. It is anecdote-heavy.

Title: The Fall of Hyperion (Hyperion Cantos, #2)
Author: Dan Simmons
My Review: Fitting ending to the pilgrims' stories. I was not expecting the plot to go in this direction, and I liked the religious tone throughout.

Title: The Burnout Society
Author: Byung-Chul Han
My Review: Short and dense. It started as a rough read since I am not used to philosophy, but it gets smoother as you go. The main ideas about the achievement society and the source of depression are quite engaging. While not sure I entirely agree with its conclusions, it really makes you think.

Title: Hyperion (Hyperion Cantos, #1)
Author: Dan Simmons
My Review: Collection of interconnected stories from unlucky pilgrims, each written in a different style. My favourites were Weintraub's story of fatherhood and Hoyt's nightmarish tale.

Title: Stories of Your Life and Others
Author: Ted Chiang
My Review: A collection of short stories with imaginative and memorable premises. My favourite was "Story of Your Life."

Title: The Golden Road: How Ancient India Transformed the World
Author: William Dalrymple
My Review: The references were impressively thorough, and the central idea was interesting. The reading was a bit rough at times, dry. Best suited to readers who enjoy dense, highly detailed history.

Title: Project Hail Mary
Author: Andy Weir
My Review: Wholesome and plausible alien story. I loved the core idea behind the problem the characters are facing, it's imaginative and unsettling to think about if it were to happen.

Title: Notes from Underground
Author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
My Review:
A self-sabotaging (yet free?) man goes against what is "rational"

Got me thinking about my own underground tendencies, but some parts were physically painful to read.
